messages.text: Jamieson claims first win in 14 years as Norris stumbles after penalty drama

metadata.summary: Scott Jamieson ended a 14-year wait for a DP World Tour title with an emotional home victory at the Nexo Championship, as overnight leader Shaun Norris faded after being given a mid-round penalty.
metadata.content: DP World Tour: Scott Jamieson wins Nexo Championship as overnight leader Shaun Norris falls short after penalty drama | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content DP World Tour: Scott Jamieson wins Nexo Championship as overnight leader Shaun Norris falls short after penalty drama Scott Jamieson finished two strokes clear of Matthew Jordan, with England's Andy Sullivan in third spot; Shaun Norris ended tied-seventh having being assessed a two-shot penalty during his final round in Scotland Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 23 August 2026 17:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the Nexo Championship, where Scott Jamieson claimed an impressive victory Scott Jamieson ended a 14-year wait for a DP World Tour title with an emotional home victory at the Nexo Championship, as overnight leader Shaun Norris faded after being given a mid-round penalty. Jamieson overturned a two-shot deficit during an eventful final round at Trump International Golf Links, where a five-under 67 saw him finish on 11 under and two strokes clear of England's Matthew Jordan. The Scotsman mixed a lone bogey with six birdies - including four in a five-hole stretch around the turn - to pull clear of a congested leaderboard and claim a first DP World Tour title since December 2012. messages.text: 'Ask him' - Emery cryptic on Watkins amid transfer interest

metadata.summary: Unai Emery gave a coy and cryptic response to questions about Ollie Watkins' absence from Aston Villa's squad for their Premier League defeat at Brighton.
metadata.content: Ollie Watkins transfer news: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery gives cryptic answer when asked about striker amid Al Hilal interest | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Ollie Watkins transfer news: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery gives cryptic answer when asked about striker amid Al Hilal interest Ollie Watkins missed Aston Villa's Premier League season-opening 4-0 defeat at Brighton; England international only returned to training this week but is also subject to transfer interest from Al Hilal, who have seen at least one bid rejected for him; Watkins is keen on a Saudi move Peter Smith Senior Football Journalist @psmithXI Sunday 23 August 2026 17:32, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 'Silence' - Unai Emery gave a cryptic interview when asked about the future of Ollie Watkins Unai Emery gave a coy and cryptic response to questions about Ollie Watkins' absence from Aston Villa's squad for their Premier League defeat at Brighton. The striker did not travel to the Amex amid transfer interest from Al Hilal . Watkins is keen on the move to Saudi Arabia and Al Hilal have seen at least one bid rejected. Villa do not want to sell Watkins but talks between the clubs continue. Watkins returned from his post-World Cup summer break in the week before the game, but, when asked to explain whether his absence was due to physical or transfer-related reasons, Emery said: "Ask him. I only can answer it by silence." Transfer Centre LIVE! | Aston Villa news

messages.text: Norris beats Antonelli to victory in Dutch GP

metadata.summary: Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli to victory in Zandvoort to claim second successive race win | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli to victory in Zandvoort to claim second successive race win Lando Norris wins Dutch Grand Prix to secure back-to-back victories; Kimi Antonelli extends overall championship lead to 59 points by finishing second; Norris reduces title-race deficit to 83 points; George Russell holds off Lewis Hamilton for third; Max Verstappen crashed out on first lap Sunday 23 August 2026 17:37, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix as Lando Norris claimed victory Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix. McLaren's Norris started on pole in Zandvoort but lost the lead to Antonelli at an early standing restart after Red Bull's Max Verstappen triggered a red flag at his home race by crashing out at the end of the first lap. After struggling to pressure Antonelli on the first stint, Norris was far quicker after switching onto a hard tyre at the first round of pit stops, and eventually passed the Mercedes after emerging from his second stop with much fresher tyres than the Italian. messages.text: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record

metadata.summary: Diamond Necklace tasted defeat for the first time as Aventure served up a reminder of her top-class credentials in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet at Deauville.
metadata.content: Deauville: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record with Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet win | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Deauville: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record with Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet win Aventure produced an upset in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet, defeating the previously-unbeaten Diamond Necklace in the Deauville Group One; also on the card, Senorita Bonita dazzled for the Simon and Ed Crisford team in the Prix Morny Sunday 23 August 2026 16:09, UK Image: Aventure claimed the honours at Deauville (photo:Zuzanna Lupa) Diamond Necklace tasted defeat for the first time as Aventure served up a reminder of her top-class credentials in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet at Deauville. Aidan O'Brien's daughter of St Mark's Basilica was expected to dazzle once again in France, as she had done when landing the Prix Marcel Boussac, Poule d'Essai Des Pouliches and Prix de Diane on her travels during what was an unbeaten six-race career to date. However, she had no answer to the experience of her Christophe Ferland-trained elder, who added to last year's Group One strike in the Prix Vermeille and earned herself a quote of 20/1 for another crack at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe from bookmakers, a race in which she finished second to Bluestocking in 2024.
